subject: scripts/qa/anomaly_audit.py run FRESH on all four july31 light sets against the CURRENT staged frames and the current cull. Per-set records: datasets/july31/set-0N/audit_work/anomaly_audit.json.

why_this_was_run.the_gap: README documents the anomaly audit as part of the per-set prep, but `run_set_chain.sh` never calls it (verified: no invocation of anomaly_audit.py in that script). Consequently `run_undistort_groups.sh` prints `dwell floor: NOT CHECKED — UNVERIFIED` on every july31 set, and the only transient data in the records was RECOVERED from a pre-reset audit at 01dd19c^ taken against a different cull.
why_this_was_run.what_this_closes: the recovered figures are now re-derived against the current cull, on this rig, with the shipped tool.

ordering_constraint_honoured.rule: set-01 was audited LAST, after the rebuild-repeat experiment completed.
ordering_constraint_honoured.why: run_undistort_groups.sh derives its dwell floor from audit_work/anomaly_audit.json and ABORTS when --group is below it. The accepted set-01 product and both rebuild arms were built with NO audit record (floor NOT CHECKED). Writing one earlier could have blocked the group=100 repeat or silently changed the group size — either way it would have stopped being a same-arm repeat.

instrument.tool: scripts/qa/anomaly_audit.py — Siril does every pixel op and every measurement (decode / green-extract / subsky / findstar); the in-house kernel does only the streak geometry + cross-frame linking no tool provides. Report-only, removal-conditioned.
instrument.mount_precondition: all four sets declare mount='fixed' in acquisition.json, so the audit's cross-frame linking ran rather than stopping
instrument.classification_model: callouts in order — aircraft (two or more PARALLEL twin trails, one airframe), satellite (a single straight continuous trail), else UNKNOWN

set-01.capture_run_note: the 83 s / 119 s rig-setup gaps segment the linking into 4 runs, and runs 1-3 are EXACTLY the 7 frames recipe.json culls (3782-3788). Run 4 is exactly the 500 stacked frames. So the audit's own segmentation isolates the culled block, and no object links across the cull boundary.

set-03.aircraft_note: the two aircraft entries at PA 33.3 / 37.2 opening on the same frame DSC_5151 are the two-parallel-trails signature of ONE airframe — the object BACKLOG:`aircraft-rejection-retest` concerns.

UNKNOWN_objects.why_this_is_stated_explicitly: an UNKNOWN is the audit's honest anomaly surface — an obstruction matching no known signature, which deserves human eyes. There are none in this session. Every one of the 18 unique objects across the four sets matched either the satellite or the aircraft callout.
UNKNOWN_objects.not_a_claim_that_the_field_is_clean: it means nothing matched the UNKNOWN branch. A transient the detector never detected would not appear as UNKNOWN either; the audit bounds what it found, not what exists.

dwell_floor_vs_the_SHIPPED_group_size.constraint: `rej g 0.3 0.05` caps GESD's outlier FRACTION at 0.30, so a transient dwelling n frames in a group of G is only eligible for rejection while n/G < 0.30. Floor = ceil(max_dwell / 0.30). MECHANISM from the tool's documented parameter, not measured here.
dwell_floor_vs_the_SHIPPED_group_size.verdict: ALL FOUR SHIPPED PRODUCTS SATISFY THEIR DWELL FLOOR. No july31 product contains a transient that was ineligible for GESD rejection on this criterion. Nothing needs rebuilding on this finding.
dwell_floor_vs_the_SHIPPED_group_size.the_margin_worth_naming: set-03 clears at 90% of the cap — floor 90 against a running group of 100. A 31-frame dweller would have exceeded 0.30 outright and GESD would have stopped treating it as an outlier at all. The margin is 4 frames of dwell.
dwell_floor_vs_the_SHIPPED_group_size.and_it_is_satisfied_BY_ARITHMETIC_ACCIDE: the group size was derived to keep every group in the GESD BAND (>50 subs); nothing in the derivation reads a dwell length, because no audit record existed for any july31 set until this run. The floor is met, and it was not computed.

reproduction_against_the_RECOVERED_pre_r.why_it_matters: the recovered audits at 01dd19c^ were taken against a DIFFERENT cull, so every margin derived from them was provisional.
reproduction_against_the_RECOVERED_pre_r.verdict: ALL FOUR REPRODUCE EXACTLY — object counts, dwell spectra, and for set-03 every object's class, position angle and frame span. The recovered figures were correct against the current cull.
reproduction_against_the_RECOVERED_pre_r.why_set01_is_unaffected_by_the_cull_at_a: its 7 culled frames sit in capture runs 1-3, which contain no detected object; its single satellite is in run 4, the stacked 500.

record_integrity_REPORTED_NOT_FIXED.finding: datasets/july31/gesd_dwell_headroom.json still carries `status: PROVISIONAL — dwell figures RECOVERED from archived audits at 01dd19c^, NOT from a fresh run ... Re-derive before relying on the margins.` That re-derivation is exactly what this run performed, and all four sets reproduced.
record_integrity_REPORTED_NOT_FIXED.not_done_here: that record was NOT edited. Per this session's boundary a defect is reported, not fixed; whether its banner is discharged is the planning session's call. Every number needed to discharge it is above.
record_integrity_REPORTED_NOT_FIXED.second_finding_unchanged: the README-vs-chain contradiction stands — run_set_chain.sh still does not call anomaly_audit.py, so a future session's set will again build with `dwell floor: NOT CHECKED` unless the audit is run by hand.

what_this_does_NOT_establish: It does NOT show any transient WAS rejected. The dwell floor is an ELIGIBILITY criterion derived from GESD's documented outlier-fraction parameter — a mechanism, not a measurement of the stacked output. Whether the aircraft actually rejected is BACKLOG:`aircraft-rejection-retest`, which needs a with/without stack pair differenced along the track, and is not answered here.
It does NOT bound undetected transients. Zero UNKNOWNs means nothing reached the UNKNOWN branch, not that nothing was missed; the detector's own sensitivity is not characterised by this run.

The dwell floor assumes a transient lands wholly inside ONE group. The groups route stacks CONSECUTIVE blocks, so that is the worst case and the right one to test — but an object straddling a group boundary is split and each part is a smaller fraction, which this arithmetic does not credit.

set-01's audit covered 507 frames while its product stacks 500. That widens the audited population rather than narrowing it, and no object touches the 7 culled frames, so the floor comparison is unaffected.
The classification is the tool's callout registry, not ground truth. An object matching the satellite signature is a single straight continuous trail; nothing here confirms it is an orbital body.
products_touched: none. anomaly_audit.py is report-only and never moves, deletes or rewrites an input frame. No stack, flat, master or baseline was written.
